targets.name: Ebenezer Scrooge
targets.description: A miserly London businessman who is transformed by four ghostly visits on Christmas Eve.
targets.physical_description: Old, thin, with a pointed nose, shrivelled cheek, red eyes, thin blue lips, and frosty white hair.
targets.summary_of_actions: Rejects Christmas, is visited by Marley and three Spirits, repents, and becomes generous.

targets.name: Jacob Marley
targets.description: Scrooge's dead business partner who returns as a ghost to warn him.
targets.physical_description: A transparent ghost bound in a long chain of cash-boxes, keys, padlocks and ledgers.
targets.summary_of_actions: Appears to Scrooge, warns him of his fate, and announces the three Spirits.

targets.name: Bob Cratchit
targets.description: Scrooge's poorly paid, good-hearted clerk.
targets.physical_description: Wears a threadbare comforter in place of a greatcoat.
targets.summary_of_actions: Works in the cold office, celebrates a humble Christmas with his family, and mourns Tiny Tim in a vision of the future.

targets.name: Mrs. Cratchit
targets.description: Bob Cratchit's wife.
targets.physical_description: Dressed in a twice-turned gown, brave in ribbons.
targets.summary_of_actions: Prepares the family's Christmas dinner and reluctantly toasts Scrooge.

targets.name: Tiny Tim
targets.description: Bob Cratchit's youngest son, sickly and kind.
targets.physical_description: A small, lame boy who carries a little crutch and has his limbs supported by an iron frame.
targets.summary_of_actions: Says 'God bless Us, Every One!' and, in a future vision, has died; after Scrooge reforms, he does not die.

targets.name: Martha Cratchit
targets.description: Bob Cratchit's eldest daughter, an apprentice at a milliner's.
targets.physical_description: Not described.
targets.summary_of_actions: Comes home late for Christmas dinner and hides to tease her father.

targets.name: Peter Cratchit
targets.description: Bob Cratchit's son.
targets.physical_description: Wears his father's oversized shirt collar.
targets.summary_of_actions: Helps with the Christmas dinner and reads to the family in the future vision.

targets.name: Belinda Cratchit
targets.description: Bob Cratchit's second daughter.
targets.physical_description: Brave in ribbons.
targets.summary_of_actions: Helps her mother lay the cloth and sweetens the apple-sauce.

targets.name: Fred
targets.description: Scrooge's cheerful nephew, son of his late sister Fan.
targets.physical_description: Handsome, with a ruddy face and sparkling eyes.
targets.summary_of_actions: Invites Scrooge to Christmas dinner, hosts a party with games, and welcomes Scrooge when he finally comes.

targets.name: Ghost of Christmas Past
targets.description: The first of the three Spirits, who shows Scrooge scenes from his own past.
targets.physical_description: A strange figure like a child yet like an old man, with a bright jet of light from its crown, white hair, and a white tunic.
targets.summary_of_actions: Shows Scrooge his lonely school days, Fezziwig's ball, and his parting with Belle.

targets.name: Ghost of Christmas Present
targets.description: The second Spirit, who shows Scrooge Christmas as it is being celebrated now.
targets.physical_description: A jolly giant in a green robe bordered with white fur, wearing a holly wreath.
targets.summary_of_actions: Shows Scrooge the Cratchits, Fred's party, and the children Ignorance and Want.

targets.name: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come
targets.description: The third and last Spirit, who shows Scrooge the future.
targets.physical_description: A solemn Phantom draped in a deep black garment, showing only one outstretched hand.
known_as: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come
targets.summary_of_actions: Silently shows Scrooge his unmourned death, his plundered belongings, and his grave.

targets.name: Mr. Fezziwig
targets.description: Scrooge's jovial former employer.
targets.physical_description: An old gentleman in a Welsh wig.
targets.summary_of_actions: Throws a joyful Christmas Eve ball for his apprentices and staff.

targets.name: Mrs. Fezziwig
targets.description: Mr. Fezziwig's wife.
targets.physical_description: One vast substantial smile.
targets.summary_of_actions: Dances with her husband at their Christmas ball.

targets.name: Belle
targets.description: Scrooge's former fiancee.
targets.physical_description: A fair young girl in a mourning-dress.
targets.summary_of_actions: Releases Scrooge from their engagement because he loves money more; later shown happily married with children.

targets.name: Fan
targets.description: Scrooge's younger sister, Fred's mother, now dead.
targets.physical_description: A little girl.
targets.summary_of_actions: Comes to bring young Scrooge home from school for Christmas.

targets.name: Dick Wilkins
targets.description: Scrooge's fellow apprentice at Fezziwig's.
targets.physical_description: Not described.
targets.summary_of_actions: Clears away the warehouse with young Scrooge for the Christmas ball.

targets.name: Old Joe
targets.description: A dealer in stolen goods in a squalid shop.
targets.physical_description: A grey-haired rascal of nearly seventy years.
targets.summary_of_actions: Buys the dead man's belongings from the charwoman, laundress, and undertaker's man.

targets.name: Mrs. Dilber
targets.description: The laundress who sells the dead Scrooge's belongings.
targets.physical_description: Not described.
targets.summary_of_actions: Brings stolen sheets, towels and clothes to Old Joe.

targets.name: Topper
targets.description: A bachelor friend at Fred's Christmas party.
targets.physical_description: Not described.
targets.summary_of_actions: Pursues the plump sister during blind man's buff.

targets.name: Caroline
targets.description: A debtor's wife in the future vision.
targets.physical_description: A mild and patient creature with a careworn face.
targets.summary_of_actions: Is relieved to hear that the man they owed money to has died.
